# sendio_domain_verification (Resource)

Checks a domain's DNS records now (`POST /domains/{id}/verify`) and, with `wait_for_verification`, waits until the domain is verified. Publish the records from `sendio_domain.records` first (for example with your DNS provider's Terraform resources). Destroying this resource changes nothing in send.io.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "sendio_domain" "mail" {
  name = "mail.example.com"
}

# Publish sendio_domain.mail.records first (for example with aws_route53_record
# or cloudflare_record), then wait for the domain to verify.
resource "sendio_domain_verification" "mail" {
  domain_id             = sendio_domain.mail.id
  wait_for_verification = true

  timeouts = {
    create = "45m"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `domain_id` (String) Id of the domain to verify.

### Optional

- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))
- `triggers` (Map of String) Arbitrary values that re-run the verification when they change (for example DNS record ids).
- `wait_for_verification` (Boolean) Wait until the domain status is `verified`, re-checking DNS every 15 seconds, up to the create timeout (default 30 minutes).

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Same as `domain_id`.
- `status` (String) Domain status after the check (refreshed on every read).
- `verified` (Boolean) Whether the domain status is `verified`.

<a id="nestedatt--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import sendio_domain_verification.mail 4ef0f1a6-2c0b-4d0e-8f0e-2b1d6a1f0c11
```
